To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in a hollow conductor wave guide open along z-axis, (ii) in the presence of a constant background magnetic field, (iii) in the special reference frame where the background field points along x or y, (iv) all the transverse electric modes are observed propagating throughout guide, while (v) all the transvere magnetic modes are absent.
waveguides, in a special class of Lorentz frames, are able to suppress or amplify the intensity of the transverse electric and magnetic modes, respectively.

(1) the presence of CPT- and/or Lorentz-violating background fields, in a special class of frames, leads to a huge suppression of the transverse magnetic modes in the spectrum of the confined electromagnetic waves; and (2) this suppression can be used to test the Standard Model Extension with a simple, inexpensive, and easily reproducible experimental apparatus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a new method for the study of CPT- and/or Lorentz- odd electrodynamics.
the study of CPT- and/or Lorentz- symmetry violations, in particular with their effects on electromagnetic waves.
the study of a new and powerful method to detect CPT- and/or Lorentz-violations, based on a simple apparatus, the hollow conductor waveguide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
waveguides are very good tools to test these effects, even if the experimental apparatus is quite simple and inexpensive.

waveguide-based tests of Lorentz and CPT symmetry are a very promising way to detect the presence of a CPT- and/or Lorentz odd background field, and that they could be used to set new stringent bounds on the parameters of the Standard Model Extension.
waveguides are an excellent tool for probing CPT and Lorentz violation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if the Standard Model Extension is correct, then the existence of a Lorentz-violating background field is a necessary condition for the propagation of electromagnetic waves in waveguides.
, if the CPT- and/or Lorentz- symmetry are not violated, the waveguide spectrum should be identical to that of the standard electrodynamics.
the Standard Model Extension predicts the existence of an effective magnetic field, which is proportional to the electric field, and which has a direction opposite to the electric field.
